attempts.answer_text: The Production Database Access SOP describes how engineers request, receive, and lose production database access [da1cdb5e0e87ad69728e9d2781239d13]. It applies to engineers needing direct read or write access to a production database, such as on-call engineers, those debugging customer issues, or running one-time data migrations, but excludes access through internal admin tools with their own audit logs and approval flows [da1cdb5e0e87ad69728e9d2781239d13]. Engineers request access via an access request form on the internal tools portal, requiring approval from the system's data owner and two engineering managers (with one from a different team) [da1cdb5e0e87ad69728e9d2781239d13]. Standard access is granted for three days and expires automatically, and engineers must have completed annual security training within the last ninety days [da1cdb5e0e87ad69728e9d2781239d13], [fa6a8fa3ff7c9abfd858f139e55ab66d]. During incidents, on-call engineers may request break-glass emergency access without standard approval, which is logged and reviewed the next business day [da1cdb5e0e87ad69728e9d2781239d13]. All access grants are logged and reviewed weekly by Security Engineering [da1cdb5e0e87ad69728e9d2781239d13], [91d4f121536a0880dff84e83193cd833]. A manager or data owner can revoke access early [91d4f121536a0880dff84e83193cd833]. Service accounts and automated jobs follow a separate process requiring sign-off from the data owner and two engineering managers, with quarterly reviews rather than automatic expiration [91d4f121536a0880dff84e83193cd833].
